reviewer_role: independent refutation of P5-03 and P5-04
scope: Read-only inspection of specification, production C/interfaces, fake hardware and simulator host; reviewed previously executed audit probe evidence. No build or test executed by this reviewer; no source changes.
approval_check: approval.md records explicit owner approval of the current revised SD and Phase 5; stale pending wording inside SD does not invalidate this baseline.

findings.reasoning: C15 and PSPEC 2/4.1 explicitly require a TRUE dust observation during avoidance to survive a later FALSE and override any paused D3 count on first Forward. detect_dust returns a transient hardware Boolean; get_inputs and decide_actions pass it only into this Tick. track_power_up ignores dust while Avoiding and retains only D3. There is no current/pending D2 latch in the inspected production files. Thus C11 preservation works but cannot satisfy C15 restart precedence. The existing executed probe uses an actual dust read on the first Stop Tick followed by nine avoidance Ticks, then Forward; its observed Start/0 and paused-count result 2 agree with the code and contradict expected Power Up/4. Current TRUE on the returning Forward Tick does restart correctly, so partial is more precise than wholly absent for C15 overall.
findings.execution_evidence: verification/probe-results.json: C15.avoidance_only_dust_return_clean expected 2 actual 0; return_remaining expected 4 actual 0; pending_overrides_paused_remaining expected 4 actual 2. C11.no_new_dust_resumes_remaining expected and actual 2. Probe source reviewed; these are earlier executed audit probes, not newly executed by this reviewer or browser/system tests.
corrections: Preserve the passing C11 no-new-dust resume path when fixing C15.
Describe the value after the restart Tick as remaining 4; the full restart count is 5 before the current Tick is consumed.
P5-03 is the concrete remembered-dust behavioral failure; avoid counting its downstream effect again as a distinct business defect in P5-04.

findings.reasoning: The approved SD section 2 expressly excludes polling only the latest values once per Tick and requires an ordered lossless received-event adapter plus event dispatch and private Sensor Store access. Existing main instead waits for a Tick then calls Controller; Controller/get_inputs poll four current values, with dust represented as a single bool. hw_interface.h exposes only old reads/wait and outputs. The simulator host accepts one four-value line per Tick and has no independent event-kind/receipt stream. The fake hardware can change current values in before_tick but has no delivery/storage path for each intermediate sensor observation. Inspected production paths and alternative-term searches found no event receiver/dispatcher, sensor readiness, D2 getter/clearer, or pending state. Therefore SD-EVENT and SD-STORE sub-obligations are absent; replacing only the power-up latch would not supply the approved input boundary. Sequential Controller execution already exists, so do not label every serialization aspect absent. Hardware transport remains B6-excluded; the missing obligation is the software boundary contract that tests/simulator must realize.
findings.absence_search: rg -n -i 'receive_input|dispatch|sensor_store|sensor_data|input_event|pending_dust|dust_pending|valid|inputs_ready|get_dust_existence|clear_pending' src include simulator/host tests/fake_hw.cpp returned no matches; full input call path, all include/src file inventory, host and fake input implementations inspected.
findings.execution_evidence: verification/probe-results.json reports 14 missing and 9 old call edges. Its C15.observed_true_false_before_tick check reads detect_dust twice using changed fake sensor values, then invokes Controller; expected Clean 2, actual 0. This is a direct legacy-function probe, not a production asynchronous event-delivery run. Absent production event delivery is established statically, not by claiming the simulator actually received and lost asynchronous events.
corrections: Replace candidate wording detect_dust(TRUE), detect_dust(FALSE) with: set fake dust TRUE, call detect_dust(void), set fake dust FALSE, call detect_dust(void). The actual function accepts no parameters; this signature mismatch itself is part of SD noncompliance.
Keep P5-04 as an approved interface/boundary divergence with a received-event loss consequence under that contract; do not claim an observed asynchronous production execution.
Count absent event reception/dispatch and private D1/D2 storage obligations separately from already present sequential execution of one Controller cycle per Tick.
Do not infer a physical sensor/interrupt/driver implementation requirement beyond B6 or require a particular hardware transport.
